title: LLM Judges as Raters: A Pre-Registered Audit of Severity, Halo, Reliability, and Version Instability in LLM Essay Scoring on Public Corpora
abstract: arXiv:2608.29517v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as essay graders in learning analytics, evaluated almost exclusively with agreement statistics. Educational measurement warns that raters also differ in severity, show halo, and drift as instruments. We treat LLM judges as raters and run a pre-registered rater-effects battery (many-facet Rasch severity, residual halo, generalizability/decision studies, cross-version shifts, differential functioning) on public corpora in two languages (ENEM/Essay-BR; ASAP): 2,377 essays, 12 judges, 4 providers, 5 version contrasts, replicated cells, released as a score tensor. Judge severity spans 219 points on ENEM's 0-1000 scale; on ASAP the panel spread is 15-33% of the score range against a between-trained-human gap near 1%. Judge-human correlations sit in an undiscriminating .47-.56 band. All five version contrasts shift severity beyond a family-wise permutation null (up to 133 points), and one judge

translated_title: 作为评分员的LLM评委：基于公开语料的LLM作文评分中严厉度、光环效应、信度与版本不稳定性的预注册审计
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在学习分析领域越来越多地被用作作文评分者，但其评估几乎完全依赖一致性统计数据。教育测量学警告说，评分员在严厉程度上存在差异，会表现出光环效应，并会随测量工具发生漂移。本研究将LLM评委视为评分员，对两种语言的公开语料库（ENEM/Essay-BR；ASAP）开展了预注册的评分员效应测试套件（多面Rasch严厉度分析、残余光环效应、概化/决策研究、跨版本偏移、差异功能分析），涵盖2,377篇作文、12个评委、4个提供商、5组版本对比及重复实验单元，并以分数张量的形式公开发布。研究发现：评委严厉度在ENEM的0-1000分制上跨度高达219分；在ASAP上，评委小组的分数差异占评分范围的15-33%，而训练有素的人类评分员之间的差距仅接近1%；评委与人类评分的相关性处于缺乏区分度的0.47-0.56区间；所有五组版本对比的严厉度变化均超出家族级置换零假设（最高达133分），且其中一个评委……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该预注册研究首次将LLM作文评委当作教育测量学中的“评分员”进行系统审计，发现不同LLM评分严厉度差异巨大（ENEM量表上跨度达219分）、存在光环效应、与人类评分相关性仅0.47-0.56，且模型版本更新会导致评分严厉度显著漂移，表明仅靠一致性统计无法可靠评估LLM评分质量。
en_tdlr: This pre-registered audit treats LLM judges as educational measurement raters, revealing vast severity differences (up to 219 points), halo effects, weak judge-human correlations (.47-.56), and significant scoring drift across model versions—demonstrating that agreement statistics alone are insufficient for evaluating LLM essay graders.
